issues: P2 — Supervisor publication failures can become false worker-integrity violations. atomic_json has no finally cleanup for its temporary file. An ordinary write/fsync error, or a handled interruption raised before os.replace, can leave a file such as a packet destination plus '.<pid>.tmp'. Master.worker then sees that supervisor-created file as a new, unapproved write. For read-only roles it necessarily raises ContinuationVeto; for editable phases a temporary file in the run directory is outside the declared write scope. This misclassifies a recoverable publication/interruption failure as worker misconduct and prevents the normal review retry or resumable interruption path. Repair atomic_json with exception-safe cleanup of its own temporary file, preserving the original destination and original exception. If partially serialized content must be retained as evidence, preserve it explicitly through a supervisor-owned recovery mechanism rather than leaving an unclassified inventory entry. Do not broadly exempt arbitrary temporary files.
